name: SerialRuntime_Initialize
algorithm: Saves REG_IME, self-writes REG_IME with its own address, registers two interrupt handlers via Func_0800307c, disables IME, clears the VBlank/serial bits pending in REG_IE/REG_IF, cycles REG_RCNT/REG_SIOCNT to select general-purpose serial mode and arms multiplayer SIOCNT bits, re-enables IME, DMAs a zero word into the SERIAL_RUNTIME block via DMA3, initializes SERIAL_RUNTIME's send_index and send/incoming/ready/pending buffer pointers into its storage[], re-enables the serial IRQ, clears SERIAL_TRANSFER/SERIAL_ACTIVE_A/B state, calls Func_0800651c, and restores the original REG_IME.
evidence: Field values, header addresses (REG_IME/REG_IE/REG_IF/REG_RCNT/REG_SIOCNT/REG_SIOCNT16/DMA3/SERIAL_RUNTIME/SERIAL_ACTIVE_A/B/SERIAL_VALUE_A/B) and struct layout all come from games/gs1/recon/en/main/serial_runtime_family.h, already shared by this owner's sibling translation-unit members (08005d10 through 0800651c); semantic values already match the reference literal pool byte-for-byte (0xff3f, 0x8000, 0x1000, 0x2000, 0x4003, 0x85000058, etc. all appear verbatim in games/gs1/asm/08005d10.s's pools), so the residual below is pure instruction-scheduling / register-allocation shape, not a value or algorithm error.

games/gs1/asm/08005d10.s (the retained byte-exact reference disassembly) shows a single `stmia r3!, {r0, r1, r2}` / `subs r3, #12` for the DMA3 descriptor write (source=&zero, destination=SERIAL_RUNTIME, control=0x85000058), with no matching `ldmia` nearby.
credible_shapes_tried: Baseline: DMA3->source/destination/control written through the TU-wide `volatile struct DmaRegisters *DMA3` macro (plain per-field volatile stores): 350/350 bytes, 117 differing halfwords -- three separate `str` instructions, no stmia.

Adopted improvement: a locally-scoped, non-volatile `struct DmaRegistersRW` alias to the same 0x040000d4 block (see in-file comment), used only for this store: 350/350 bytes, 115 differing halfwords. Confirmed via alchemy-gcc/gs1cc/gcc/config/arm/arm.c's store_multiple_sequence (~line 3572) that its consecutive-store combiner explicitly excludes MEM_VOLATILE_P operands, so the volatile qualifier alone was sufficient to suppress any chance of a combined store; removing it is necessary but, on this owner, not sufficient (below).

All 6 permutations of the source/destination/control field-store statement order (with the non-volatile alias): all either matched the adopted 115-differing-halfword result (src,dst,ctl / dst,src,ctl / dst,ctl,src / ctl,dst,src) or regressed to 122 (src,ctl,dst / ctl,src,dst). None produced a combined stmia.

A local `struct SerialRuntime *runtime = SERIAL_RUNTIME;` (function-scope and block-scoped variants) reused directly across send_index/send_buffer/incoming_buffer/ready_buffer/pending_buffer: measurably closer instruction shape (wrong_instructions dropped from 84 to 66) but candidate shrank to 346 bytes vs the 350-byte reference -- GCC reused the cached pointer directly instead of reference's repeated `mov r2,ip` / `mov r3,ip` / `mov r4,ip` copies, so this shape is 2 instructions shorter than the reference and was rejected as a length mismatch.

Re-deriving `runtime = SERIAL_RUNTIME;` at the top of each loop iteration/statement (forcing fresh reloads instead of one cached copy): restored the 350-byte length but regressed to 122 differing halfwords -- worse than the adopted non-volatile-alias draft.
compiler_backend_evidence: Read alchemy-gcc/gs1cc/gcc/config/arm/arm.c directly for this owner. Two independent Thumb code paths can ever emit the `stmia` mnemonic: (1) thumb_output_move_mem_multiple (~9425-9469), reached only from thumb_expand_movstrqi for a genuine memory-to-memory block copy, which always emits a paired `ldmia` immediately before the `stmia` as one indivisible RTL insn -- ruled out here since the reference has no nearby ldmia (already documented, for the sibling owner 0800300c, in 0800300c.json's compiler_backend_evidence); and (2) the generic consecutive-store combiner reachable from store_multiple_sequence (~3572), which merges same-base, ascending, adjacent-offset word stores into one `stmia`/`stmib`/`stmda`/`stmdb` but explicitly bails out with `if (MEM_VOLATILE_P (operands[nops + i])) return 0;` ('Don't reorder volatile memory references'). Path (2) is therefore only reachable when DMA3 is treated as non-volatile, which is what the locally-scoped `DmaRegistersRW` alias in this file provides. Even so, on this owner the combiner never actually fires: the freshly-compiled .s (scratch/candidate-show/08005d10/08005d10.s) shows the destination-value store scheduled after an intervening `b`-over-literal-pool from the other two field stores, so the three stores are never adjacent in the emitted instruction stream for the combiner's peephole to match, regardless of which of the 6 field-order permutations was tried.
remaining: 115 of 350 candidate bytes' worth of halfwords differ, concentrated in two scheduler-level residuals rather than any remaining semantic/value/type error: (1) the function's opening block (interrupt_enable = REG_IME; ime_reg = &REG_IME; *ime_reg = ...; then the first Func_0800307c(7,0,Func_08006240) call) -- the reference's Haifa list scheduler places `sub sp, #4` and `adds r7, r3, #0` (saving interrupt_enable into the callee-saved r7) immediately after the REG_IME read and before the call-argument setup, while every source-statement ordering tried here instead hoists the independent `ldr r5, =Func_08006240` and the r0/r1 argument movs earlier, deferring `sub sp, #4` until just before the `bl`; both orderings are semantically and length-identical schedules of the same instruction set; and (2) the DMA3-descriptor-write region and everything downstream of it through the incoming/ready/pending-buffer loop and the final SERIAL_ACTIVE_A/B / SERIAL_VALUE_A/B stores, where the reference caches the SERIAL_RUNTIME base pointer once in `ip` and re-derives it into r1/r2/r3/r4 via cheap `mov` copies at each subsequent use, producing a register-naming pattern (and, per the literal-pool placement above, an unreachable stmia) that this owner's ordinary field-store and locally-scoped-pointer shapes were not able to reproduce byte-for-byte; the resulting register-name (not value) mismatches then cascade, unchanged in kind, through the rest of the function. No length mismatch remains (candidate_bytes == owner_bytes == 350); the residual is pure instruction ordering / register allocation inside otherwise-correct code.
notes: No inline assembly, fixed-register variable, compiler barrier, forbidden ABI, copied instruction bytes, or compiler modification was used. The `DmaRegistersRW` type/macro is a locally-scoped, non-volatile alias for the same 0x040000d4 DMA3 register block already declared (volatile) in the shared serial_runtime_family.h; it does not modify that header or any other owner's source.
